passage:
Dear Zubin bhai,
You said never to decide anything when I'm this angry, so I'm writing to say I listened. Yesterday in the physics test I saw my friend Sameer copying from under his desk. I almost stormed to Sir's table right then. My hands were shaking and my head was full of speeches. Instead I went home, ate dinner and did nothing. I slept badly, but by morning the anger had shrunk. I realised I would have been shouting, and a rushed complaint might have sounded more like revenge than fairness. So here's my plan: talk to Sameer privately at lunch and ask him to tell Sir himself, and if nothing changes by next week, I'll tell Sir myself. Thank you for the rule.
Your cousin,
Akash

qa.q: When will Akash tell Sir if nothing changes?
qa.a: Akash will tell Sir if nothing changes by next week.

qa.q: How did Akash feel right after seeing Sameer copy?
qa.a: Akash felt angry, with shaking hands and a head full of speeches.

qa.q: What could Akash do if Sameer refuses to talk?
qa.a: Akash could take it to the teacher calmly, as planned, since one fair chance has already been given.

qa.q: How might Sameer feel when Akash talks to him privately?
qa.a: Sameer may feel surprised and nervous, but a quiet talk lets Sameer respond without being shamed in front of the class.

grounding: A student holds back for a night, cools down and decides on a private conversation followed by a teacher if nothing changes, instead of a rushed angry act.

Irawati, you asked why I didn't go straight to Ma'am about Pallav. I'm Minakshi, and honestly, I almost did.
I saw him copy in the Hindi test, and I was so angry. I'd studied the whole weekend, and he was just reading off his palm. By the time I got home I'd typed a message to Ma'am, very long, with words like “shameless”.
But Amma has a rule: never send anything important when you're boiling. So I put the phone in the drawer and slept on it.
Next morning I read the message again, and it sounded like revenge, not concern. So I deleted it. I decided I'd talk to Pallav first, privately, and if he did it again, I'd tell Ma'am calmly, just the facts.
I talked to him at lunch. He was embarrassed and said it wouldn't happen again. So far it hasn't. If it does, I know what I'll say, and it won't sound like that message.

qa.q: What words did Minakshi's first message include?
How did Minakshi feel reading the message the next morning?
qa.a: Minakshi felt uncomfortable and calmer, seeing that it sounded like revenge rather than concern.

qa.q: What might Minakshi do if Pallav copies again?
qa.a: Tell Ma'am calmly with just the facts, as planned, rather than with the angry words of that first night.

qa.q: How might Pallav have felt when Minakshi spoke to him at lunch?
qa.a: Pallav was embarrassed, but probably relieved to be spoken to privately rather than reported in anger.

grounding: Shows a student holding back for a night, cooling down, and choosing a private talk first and a teacher only if nothing changes, since a rushed act would have been angrier.

I'm Joseph, and Uma and I walk home together, so I saw her on the day she found out. She had seen Nisha, her closest friend, copy the answers in the chemistry test. She was furious on the walk home, kicking stones, saying she would tell Mr Kapoor first thing tomorrow, in front of everyone if she had to.
At her gate she stopped and said, “No. I'll decide tomorrow. If I decide now, I'll do something mean.” She went in.
The next morning she was quiet. On the walk she said she'd thought about it, and the plan was: talk to Nisha alone at break, and if Nisha didn't stop, go to Mr Kapoor, but calmly, just facts.
At break I saw them on the steps. Nisha was nodding. I don't know exactly what was said. But Uma didn't go to the staffroom that day, and she didn't seem angry any more.

qa.q: Who did Uma say she would tell first thing?
How did Uma seem the next morning, compared with the walk home?
qa.a: Uma seemed quiet and calmer, the fury of the evening replaced by a clear plan.

qa.q: What else could Uma do if Nisha keeps copying?
qa.a: Go to Mr Kapoor calmly with just the facts, as planned, rather than in anger in front of everyone.

qa.q: How might Nisha have experienced the talk on the steps?
qa.a: Nisha was likely embarrassed but relieved to hear it privately from a friend rather than being exposed in front of the class.

grounding: A classmate sees a student hold back for a night, cool down, and choose a private talk with the friend first and a teacher only if nothing changes.
